title: gpu-commit-impact-tracker-and-ci-prioritization-spec v1
author: Aisha Ramanathan
content:
Summary:
This spec describes the GPU Commit Impact Tracker (GCIT): a small service plus CI prioritization layer that estimates how much infra cost and SLO risk a PR or commit carries, and routes CI and preflight testing based on that estimate. The intent is to stop burning GPU CI on low-risk changes, catch risky changes earlier, and give high-risk changes higher-fidelity testing without growing total CI capacity.

Goals:
- Cut GPU CI waste by 30% within 6 months while holding or improving post-merge latency SLOs.
- Catch infra regressions (latency, memory, eviction rate) earlier in the pipeline.
- Send each PR to the right test band (GPU simulator unit tests, small-instance smoke, full mixed-precision perf) based on predicted impact.
- Keep the score and routing decision transparent and auditable.

Scope:
- Covers repos that create or modify serving runtime artifacts, quantized kernels, scheduler code, or tenant-facing config affecting batching/eviction.
- Out of scope: docs-only changes, front-end-only UI work, and non-inference tooling unless deployment manifests are touched.

Architecture overview:
1) GCIT webhook (GitHub App) receives PR metadata and a lightweight diff summary.
2) A stateless impact classifier computes a risk score and recommended band from rules plus features: touched files, module ownership, recent telemetry deltas, heuristic cost estimate, and historical flake/regression signals.
3) The CI router (Buildkite step or GitHub Actions dispatcher) maps band -> pipeline and enforces concurrency buckets.
4) A telemetry exporter logs decisions, downstream results and post-merge metrics for retraining and policy tuning.

Components:
- Diff Analyzer: file-glob fingerprinting. Known fingerprints: kernel/ops/*.cu, runtime/kernel_selector/*, quantization/*.py, iac/*.tf, charts/*.yaml. Also records added/removed LOC and changed binaries.
- Feature Extractor: repo owner, touched modules, LOC, CUDA line counts, public config flag references, and whether batching or KV cache paths are touched.
- Rules Engine: ordered deterministic rules that short-circuit the model for safety-critical changes (anything touching preemption/fallback code is HIGH risk).
- Scoring Model: small weighted model for alpha (logistic regression or small XGBoost), weights kept in config with online adjustment from telemetry.
- Router: Buildkite plugin mapping bands to pipelines. Bands: fast-sim, smoke-small, perf-full, infra-ops.

Scoring heuristics (example):
- Base score = 0
- +6 for changes under runtime/kernel_selector/ or kernel ops
- +5 for CUDA/C++ file changes (by extension)
- +4 for Terraform manifests under infra/ or iac/
- +3 if batching/kv-cache keywords appear in the diff
- +2 if LOC > 200
- -2 for docs/tests-only changes
- Force HIGH risk for changes to preemption, warm-pool, tenant-scheduling or HSM integration paths.

Bands and routing:
- fast-sim (score <= 2): unit tests plus CPU microbench simulator. Max pipeline runtime: 15m. For low-risk changes such as small config edits.
- smoke-small (score 3-6): one small-GPU smoke job (p3.2xlarge equivalent), basic perf check and integration smoke. Runtime: 1h.
- perf-full (score >= 7 or rule override): full multi-config GPU matrix with mixed-precision kernel validation, quantization regression checks and SLO synthetic traces. Runtime: 3–6h.
- infra-ops (manual triage): raised when secrets, network policy changes or Terraform changes needing approval are detected. An infra-approver must sign off before CI continues.

Test matrix mapping:
- runtime/* changed -> perf-full
- kernel/*.cu changed -> perf-full plus quant matrix
- iac/terraform/*.tf changed -> infra-ops (plan + state-check job)
- docs-only -> fast-sim

Terraform / IaC requirements:
- Tag modules that affect warm-pool or warm-up seeding with gcit_sensitive = true; the Diff Analyzer treats them as HIGH risk.
- CI runs terraform plan | jq to list changed resources; any sensitive resource marks the PR infra-ops.
- Modules may pass gcit_impact_metadata = { owner = "team-x", impact = "high|medium|low" } (stringified map), which the Diff Analyzer reads when present.

Metrics:
- GCIT.decisions.total (labels: repo, team, band)
- postmerge.mean_p99_ms_delta
- ci.gpu_minutes_saved_by_band (estimated)
- Count of post-merge incidents traced to PRs routed to fast-sim (false negatives)
- gcit.telemetry.rows (weekly retraining dataset size)

SLOs and thresholds:
- Decision latency: GCIT must score and respond within 30s for 95% of PRs.
- Routing correctness: target 90% recall on HIGH-risk PRs, measured against historical incidents over a rolling 90d window.
- GPU CI savings: 30% fewer unnecessary perf-full runs within 6 months.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (canary, 2 weeks): dry-run on one low-risk repo (ci-inference-sandbox); GCIT labels PRs but does not alter pipelines.
- Phase 1 (staged, 6 weeks): routing on for 5 repos across infra, runtime and tooling, with slow-fail (routing failure falls back to perf-full).
- Phase 2 (wide, 8 weeks): onboard remaining runtime and model-serving teams; terraform gating for prod infra repos with manual approvers.
- Phase 3 (optimizing): tune weights, add heuristics, wire up the retraining loop.

Oncall runbook (post-merge regression traced to routing):
1) PagerDuty alert gcit-regression-signal; first-line oncall triages within 60m.
2) Reproduce: find the PR and rerun the full perf matrix on its commit.
3) Mitigate: revert or hotfix by severity. Revert via GitHub, then the 'emergency' CI pipeline runs perf-full on the revert commit.
4) Root cause: tag whether the score (model/rules) or the test matrix was at fault.
5) Postmortem: owner team writes it and links it for the retraining dataset.

Router mapping YAML:

router:
  bands:
    - name: fast-sim
      max_runtime: 15m
      concurrency_bucket: low
    - name: smoke-small
      max_runtime: 60m
      concurrency_bucket: medium
    - name: perf-full
      max_runtime: 6h
      concurrency_bucket: high
    - name: infra-ops
      requires_approver: true

Local testing:
$ gcit-diff-analyzer --repo . --base main --head feature/fast-path --out features.json
$ gcit-score --features features.json --config /etc/gcit/weights.yaml

Ownership:
- Primary owner: eng-infra CI/CD team (oncall alias: eng-infra-ci)
- Secondary reviewers: runtime-team@redwood.ai, quantization@redwood.ai
- SRE integration owner: Evan Li

Open questions:
- Should some kernel-level changes require a canary on dedicated capacity? (cost vs safety)
- How to handle cross-repo PRs atomically? Current plan: detect and escalate to infra-ops.

Appendix A — Example weights:
weights:
  kernel_selector: 4
  cuda_file: 5
  terraform_sensitive: 6
  batching_keyword: 3
  loc_threshold: 2

Appendix B — Dashboard queries:
- Decision rate by band (last 30d): sum(GCIT.decisions.total) by band
- Post-merge regressions traced to GCIT: sum(alerts.where(label="gcit_regression"))

Notes:
GCIT is conservative by default and will be tuned with telemetry. The goal is to catch expensive, silent regressions before production, not to slow developers down. Questions go to the owners above or as a PR against this page.
